roster.name: Mega Gengar
roster.rationale: Mega Gengar at 18 points is the strongest single pick on the board. Shadow Tag is one of the most warping abilities in VGC doubles — it lets you permanently remove one of the opponent's six Pokémon from play each game, creating an insurmountable numbers advantage. With 170 base Special Attack and 130 Speed, it's also a legitimate game-ending special sweeper on its own. It forces every opponent to either carry a Ghost immunity (which is scarce) or play around the trap.

roster.name: Pelipper
roster.rationale: Incineroar was already taken, so pivoting to Pelipper at 18 points — within the 19-point cap. Pelipper provides Drizzle rain support that pairs well with Mega Gengar's Ghost/Poison typing and opens up rain-boosted coverage options. At 18 pts it leaves 64 points for the remaining 8 picks: Garchomp(18), Clefable(15), Torkoal(15), Meowscarada(12), and budget fillers Absol/Pikachu/Emolga/Castform(4).

roster.name: Garchomp
roster.rationale: Garchomp at 18 points fits perfectly within the 19-point cap and continues the pre-planned roster. It brings Dragon/Ground typing with excellent 130 Attack and 102 Speed, providing a strong physical offensive pivot that complements Mega Gengar's special offense and Pelipper's rain support. No species conflicts with existing picks, and the remaining 46 points exactly cover the planned Clefable (15), Torkoal (15), Meowscarada (12), and budget filler (Absol, Pikachu, Emolga, Castform at 1 each).

roster.name: Clefable
roster.rationale: Clefable at 15 points fills the critical special-wall role on a team that currently lacks a dedicated bulky special defender. Its Fairy typing covers Garchomp's Dragon weakness, and Unaware lets it shut down opposing setup sweepers and special attackers that threaten Pelipper and Garchomp. At 15 it leaves 31 points for 6 remaining picks, keeping the roster plan on track.

roster.name: Toxapex
roster.rationale: Toxapex is the premier physical wall and pivot in Champions VGC. With Regenerator, Mold Breaker, and massive 152/142 defenses, it patches the physical frailty my team currently has behind Clefable. It also provides crucial Poison/Water coverage, a Haze option to shut down opposing setup, and Regenerator pivoting to keep momentum. At 8 points it leaves 23 for 5 remaining slots.

roster.name: Meowscarada
roster.rationale: Meowscarada fills the critical speed-control and fast-offensive-threat slot at only 12 points. Its 123 base Speed with Protean (or Overgrow) gives me a revenge killer and late-game cleaner that none of my current picks provide. It pairs well with Pelipper's rain for wallbreaking and covers Garchomp's Dragon/Ground overlap by threatening bulky Water- and Ground-types from the special side.

roster.name: Skarmory
roster.rationale: The team's most urgent need is a hazard setter to support Garchomp and Mega Gengar switch-ins. Skarmory at 3 points is the cheapest effective option, providing Stealth Rock, Spikes, a Steel/Flying physical wall that checks Fairy and Ice attacks aimed at Clefable and Meowscarada, and Whirlwind phazing. This leaves 8 points for 3 remaining picks to fill speed control and pivot slots.

roster.name: Scrafty
roster.rationale: Scrafty at 3 points gives me Intimidate for crucial speed control in doubles (dropping both opponents' Attack on switch-in), solid physical bulk (115/115), and Dark/Fighting coverage that complements my team's many special attackers. It pairs naturally with Skarmory—Intimidate softens physical threats while Skarmory walls physical attackers and can set up Tailwind or Whirlwind. At 3 points it leaves 5 points for my final two slots.

roster.name: Jolteon
roster.rationale: Jolteon at 4 points fills my biggest gap: speed and pivoting. At 130 base Speed it outruns nearly everything on my current roster, Electric STAB handles the Water and Flying types that threaten Garchomp and Pelipper, and Volt Switch generates momentum in doubles. It leaves 1 point for a final utility pick.

roster.name: Forretress
roster.rationale: Forretress at 1 point fills the hazard support role I identified as a need. Bug/Steel typing with Sturdy and Overcoat gives me a reliable physical wall that can also set and remove hazards—critical in a roster that otherwise lacks dedicated entry hazard control. It rounds out the team's defensive backbone alongside Skarmory and Toxapex.

roster.name: Mega Charizard Y
roster.rationale: Mega Charizard Y immediately establishes a dominant weather archetype, setting permanent sun with Drought while packing devastating spread Heat Waves and solar utility. At 20 points, it anchors our offensive core with top-tier Special Attack and sun-boosting capability without pricing us out of our remaining 9 slots.

roster.name: Venusaur
roster.rationale: Securing Venusaur gives us the premier Chlorophyll sweeper under Mega Charizard Y's Drought sun, unlocking devastating offensive pressure and sleep utility. At 13 points, it leaves us with 67 points for our remaining 8 picks, maintaining a very healthy budget average. It forms an immediate powerhouse core with Charizard Y while leaving plenty of room for tailwind, redirection, and defensive pivots.

roster.name: Torkoal
roster.rationale: Torkoal provides an essential secondary sun setter and physical support option, complementing Mega Charizard Y's weather archetype while maximizing Venusaur's Chlorophyll speed in doubles. At 15 points, it fits comfortably within budget constraints and solidifies our weather-dependent core.

roster.name: Corviknight
roster.rationale: Corviknight provides an incredible bulky pivot, Tailwind speed control, and crucial defensive utility (defog/Iron Defense/Body Press or steel/flying typing) to complement our sun core. At 13 points, it leaves us with 39 points for our remaining 6 picks, maintaining excellent budget flexibility.

roster.name: Arcanine
roster.rationale: Arcanine provides a reliable Intimidate user and physical fire-type pivot that shores up our defensive rotation against steel and ice threats. At 11 points, it leaves us with 28 points for our remaining 5 picks while perfectly complementing our sun core.

roster.name: Basculegion-Male
roster.rationale: We secure Basculegion for 19 points, giving us an explosive Swift Swim and Adaptability rain/sun-flexible sweeper that breaks through Water resists and answers opposing Water-types. This adds crucial offensive speed control and cleaning potential to complement our sun core (Mega Charizard Y, Torkoal, Venusaur) and defensive backbone (Corviknight, Arcanine).

roster.name: Rotom
roster.rationale: At only 2 points, Rotom fits comfortably into our remaining 9-point budget while preserving flexibility for our final 3 picks. Its Electric typing and Levitate ability give us a crucial speed control option (Thunder Wave/Volt Switch) and an invaluable defensive pivot against water and flying threats that pressure our sun core.

roster.name: Bellibolt
roster.rationale: Bellibolt costs 4 points, leaving us with 3 points for our final 2 picks, and provides a bulky Electric-type pivot with Electromorphosis to absorb hits and apply offensive pressure, rounding out our defensive needs.

roster.name: Ampharos
roster.rationale: Ampharos is an available 1-point Electric-type Pokémon that fits our remaining budget of 3 points for 2 picks while leaving 2 points for our final selection. It provides useful Electric-type utility and bulk to round out our roster depth.

roster.name: Aggron
roster.rationale: Aggron costs 2 points, perfectly exhausting our remaining budget while adding a sturdy Steel/Rock physical wall with Sturdy and Rock Head to round out our 10-Pokémon roster. It provides valuable defensive typing and physical utility against threats that exploit our fire-heavy core.

roster.name: Mega Tyranitar
roster.rationale: Mega Tyranitar answers both drafted Megas in one slot: Sand Stream strips Charizard Y's sun while Rock STAB threatens a 4× OHKO, and Dark STAB punches through Mega Gengar's Shadow Tag. At 16 points with 100/150/120 bulk and 164 base Attack, it's a dominant weather-setter that anchors a sand archetype. The name riffs on sand as 'grit' — equal parts inevitability, resilience, and a little bit of attitude.

roster.name: Excadrill
roster.rationale: Excadrill is the foundational Sand Rush sweeper that makes Mega Tyranitar's Sand Stream a win condition. With 88 base Speed doubling to an effective 176+ in sand, it outspeeds nearly everything unboosted. At 13 points it's excellent value and no other coach has a sand setter to contest it — but grabbing it now secures the core before anyone considers a denial pick.

roster.name: Farigiraf
roster.rationale: Farigiraf is the ideal speed-control anchor for my sand core. Armor Tail protects both TTar and Excadrill from Fake Out (Incineroar is already drafted), Prankster Taunt/Tailwind (Whimsicott drafted), and Grassy Glide, while Trick Room gives me an alternate mode when Sand Rush gets neutralized by opposing weather or Tailwind. At 110 SpA it also fills my urgent need for a special attacker — Hyper Voice/Psychic coverage complements the physical sand duo perfectly.

roster.name: Dragapult
roster.rationale: Dragapult (14) gives my sand core exactly what it needs: a Fighting immunity to cover Mega Tyranitar's 4x weakness, 142 Speed for control outside of sand, and a versatile special/physical attacking profile with U-turn pivoting. Ghost typing also blocks Fake Out, stacking with Farigiraf's Armor Tail to shut down priority-reliant teams. At 14 points it leaves 39 for 6 picks (6.5 avg), keeping budget healthy for a Water answer and depth pieces.

roster.name: Rotom-Wash
roster.rationale: Rotom-Wash (14) is my top priority — it patches the Water matchup that threatens Excadrill and Tyranitar, provides a crucial Ground immunity via Levitate alongside Excadrill, and adds a Volt Switch pivot that operates in both fast mode and Trick Room. It also fills the secondary special attacker role. Fairy Aura Borealis (27 pts) and Prank Sinatra (40 pts) both pick before me again and could snipe it, so I secure it now.

roster.name: Tinkaton
roster.rationale: Tinkaton (11) gives me Fairy/Steel defensive glue that patches both my Dragon and Fairy weaknesses — crucial against Mega Floette's Fairy Aura and opposing Dragons. Mold Breaker Fake Out ignores Armor Tail, Gigaton Hammer is a 160 BP nuke, and its support movepool (Knock Off, Thunder Wave, Encore, Stealth Rock, screens) provides enormous role compression at a fair price, leaving 14 points for 4 remaining slots.

roster.name: Snorlax
roster.rationale: Snorlax (8) is the premier TR abuser left on the board. Base 30 Speed and 160 HP make it a perfect partner for Farigiraf's Trick Room, while Thick Fat patches Fire/Ice weaknesses that threaten the sand core. It gives the TR mode real knockout power that the roster currently lacks, and at 8 points it leaves exactly 6 points for the final three picks—enough for budget sand backup plus role players.

roster.name: Sandaconda
roster.rationale: Sandaconda at 2 is the ideal budget sand backup. With Sand Spit, it sets sand passively just by taking a hit — no turn wasted — keeping Excadrill's Sand Rush online if Ttar goes down or can't be brought. It also compresses Ground coverage and physical bulk into a cheap slot. Leaves 4 points for the final 2 picks, preserving maximum flexibility for a Grass answer (Roserade at 4, Sceptile at 3, or Scovillain at 3) plus a 1-point role-player.

roster.name: Sceptile
roster.rationale: Sceptile (3 pts) gives me fast special Grass offense at base 120 Speed, covering bulky Waters and Grounds that otherwise wall my sand core. Unburden enables terrain-seed or berry sets that outrun the entire unboosted meta, and its movepool (Leaf Storm, Focus Blast, Earth Power, Dragon Pulse, Shed Tail) adds both breaking power and utility. Leaves 1 point for the final slot.

roster.name: Camerupt
roster.rationale: Camerupt completes the TR mode alongside Farigiraf and Snorlax, bringing Fire/Ground STAB that my roster completely lacks. Solid Rock patches its bulk, Eruption devastates under TR at full HP, and Earth Power hits Rock/Water switch-ins. It also absorbs Electric moves for Rotom-Wash and punishes Steel-types that wall Snorlax, giving the TR mode real offensive teeth against both sun and balance teams.

roster.name: Incineroar
roster.rationale: Incineroar is the most reliable VGC staple on the board and the best value at 18 points: its Intimidate, Fake Out, and Parting Shot give every team a defensive and tempo anchor that the three offensive Megas already taken by rivals (Gengar, Charizard Y, Tyranitar) do not provide. Its Dark typing also helps it shrug off the Ghost/Dark/Fire threats my opponents drafted while offering redirection to shield my own wincons. Securing it now locks in a flexible core piece and leaves 82 points across nine remaining picks.

roster.name: Mega Metagross
roster.rationale: Mega Metagross gives us a premier Steel/Psychic wincon with huge bulk and Tough Claws, resisting Fairy (Floette), Dragon, and Rock while serving as a pivot against the trapped Gengar and sand/sun cores. At 17 points it fits our budget and leaves ample room for speed control and support picks later.

roster.name: Noivern
roster.rationale: Noivern is the cheapest fast Tailwind user (123 Speed) left on the board, directly filling my stated #1 need of team speed control so my slow Incineroar/Metagross core can out-pace the fast sun, Gengar, and Whimsicott threats. It also brings Taunt (shuts Prankster/Whimsicott), Boomburst pressure, and U-turn pivoting, all at only 9 points to preserve budget for a bulky Water and redirection later.

roster.name: Azumarill
roster.rationale: Azumarill is the cornerstone of my anti-sun plan: Thick Fat halves Fire/Ice so it walls Drought's CharY/Torkoal core, and as Water/Fairy it also pressures Archaludon and resists Fairy. It doubles as a redirection target for Alcremie and brings Play Rough/Aqua Jet priority. I take it now because six opponent picks occur before my next turn and this unique profile is the piece I least want to lose (Grit Happens could grab it, and my sun matchup has no other clean answer).

roster.name: Aegislash
roster.rationale: Dragapult is gone (taken by Grit Happens), so my planned Ghost/Shadow Tag answer must change; Aegislash is the best available Ghost type and also a Steel wall that resists Fairy (key vs Fairy Aura's Floette/Archaludon/Sneasler) while hitting Gholdengo and Mega Gengar super effectively. It fills the Shadow Tag-immunity hole and adds a bulky win condition, and at 14 it leaves 30 points for my remaining five picks (Alcremie redirection, a Fighting attacker, and fillers).

roster.name: Alcremie
roster.rationale: Alcremie is the only remaining Follow Me user (plus Aroma Veil) and is essential to shield my slow win-cons Mega Metagross and Aegislash from opposing priority and Prankster disruption; at 4 points it preserves budget for a Fighting-type and fillers. Securing it now prevents Prank Sinatra or Grit Happens from poaching the lone redirection option during the six picks before my next turn.

roster.name: Infernape
roster.rationale: Infernape fills the planned Fighting slot with a fast (108 Spe) attacker and Mach Punch priority to clean up Tyranitar, Archaludon, Snorlax, and Tinkaton, while its Fire STAB pressures the league's many Steel walls. It resists the Dynamos' sun-boosted Fire attacks (unlike a Steel/Fighting pick) and the 7-cost leaves 19 points for the three fillers still needed.

roster.name: Gengar
roster.rationale: Gengar is the cheapest available Ghost attacker (8 pts) and directly fills my noted need for offensive pressure; its 110 Speed / 130 SpA lets it threaten slower cores while Aegislash and Mega Metagross already wall Shadow Tag Mega Gengar. This leaves 11 points for two final fillers (speed/utility + a cheap body).

roster.name: Eelektross
roster.rationale: I'm locking in Eelektross now because Prank Sinatra (5 pts, 2 picks) could snipe this exact 3-point value before my final selection, while Liepard (8) is safe since no other coach can afford it. Eelektross's Levitate gives my roster a third Ground-immune pivot against the league's Excadrill/Garchomp/Sandaconda core, plus useful Electric coverage. My last pick will be Liepard, whose Prankster utility (Encore/Taunt/Thunder Wave/Fake Out) balances my attacker-heavy squad.

roster.name: Liepard
roster.rationale: Liepard is the only remaining option that exactly fits my 8-point budget and completes the planned 10-Pokémon roster; it supplies Prankster utility (Taunt/Encore/Thunder Wave) and Unburden speed control plus a Ground-immune Dark body alongside Noivern and Eelektross. This finalizes my team with 0 points left.

I take it now because six opponent picks occur before my next turn and this unique profile is the piece I least want to lose (Grit Happens could grab it, and my sun matchup has no other clean answer).

draftRoster.name: Aegislash
draftRoster.rationale: Dragapult is gone (taken by Grit Happens), so my planned Ghost/Shadow Tag answer must change; Aegislash is the best available Ghost type and also a Steel wall that resists Fairy (key vs Fairy Aura's Floette/Archaludon/Sneasler) while hitting Gholdengo and Mega Gengar super effectively. It fills the Shadow Tag-immunity hole and adds a bulky win condition, and at 14 it leaves 30 points for my remaining five picks (Alcremie redirection, a Fighting attacker, and fillers).

draftRoster.name: Alcremie
draftRoster.rationale: Alcremie is the only remaining Follow Me user (plus Aroma Veil) and is essential to shield my slow win-cons Mega Metagross and Aegislash from opposing priority and Prankster disruption; at 4 points it preserves budget for a Fighting-type and fillers. Securing it now prevents Prank Sinatra or Grit Happens from poaching the lone redirection option during the six picks before my next turn.

draftRoster.name: Infernape
draftRoster.rationale: Infernape fills the planned Fighting slot with a fast (108 Spe) attacker and Mach Punch priority to clean up Tyranitar, Archaludon, Snorlax, and Tinkaton, while its Fire STAB pressures the league's many Steel walls. It resists the Dynamos' sun-boosted Fire attacks (unlike a Steel/Fighting pick) and the 7-cost leaves 19 points for the three fillers still needed.

draftRoster.name: Gengar
draftRoster.rationale: Gengar is the cheapest available Ghost attacker (8 pts) and directly fills my noted need for offensive pressure; its 110 Speed / 130 SpA lets it threaten slower cores while Aegislash and Mega Metagross already wall Shadow Tag Mega Gengar. This leaves 11 points for two final fillers (speed/utility + a cheap body).

draftRoster.name: Eelektross
draftRoster.rationale: I'm locking in Eelektross now because Prank Sinatra (5 pts, 2 picks) could snipe this exact 3-point value before my final selection, while Liepard (8) is safe since no other coach can afford it. Eelektross's Levitate gives my roster a third Ground-immune pivot against the league's Excadrill/Garchomp/Sandaconda core, plus useful Electric coverage. My last pick will be Liepard, whose Prankster utility (Encore/Taunt/Thunder Wave/Fake Out) balances my attacker-heavy squad.

draftRoster.name: Liepard
draftRoster.rationale: Liepard is the only remaining option that exactly fits my 8-point budget and completes the planned 10-Pokémon roster; it supplies Prankster utility (Taunt/Encore/Thunder Wave) and Unburden speed control plus a Ground-immune Dark body alongside Noivern and Eelektross. This finalizes my team with 0 points left.

roster.name: Whimsicott
roster.rationale: Whimsicott is the best first-pick glue piece: Prankster Tailwind, Encore, Taunt, Helping Hand, and weather manipulation give it immediate value beside almost any future core. It also contests the existing Mega Charizard Y and Mega Tyranitar weather plans without locking me into one weather, while its Fairy typing and fast disruption help against Mega Gengar and Incineroar. At 19 points it is expensive, but its broad support package should remain draftable in nearly every matchup.

roster.name: Gholdengo
roster.rationale: Gholdengo is the best independent high-output partner for Whimsicott: Tailwind enables its strong spread Make It Rain, while its Steel/Ghost typing gives the roster a crucial Fairy resistance and multiple immunities. Good as Gold also blocks common status and disruption, and it pressures Mega Floette, opposing Fairy cores, and Tyranitar without committing the team to sun or sand. At 16 points, it preserves enough budget to fill the remaining roster with specialized support and counterplay.

roster.name: Gyarados
roster.rationale: Gyarados efficiently fills several urgent gaps at only 11 points: it provides Intimidate, a durable Water-type answer to the opposing sun cores, and a strong physical win condition alongside Whimsicott’s Tailwind. Dragon Dance, Taunt, Helping Hand support, and flexible Water/Flying coverage give it useful play into sand, Incineroar-style positioning, and bulky teams without making the roster weather-dependent.

roster.name: Volcarona
roster.rationale: Volcarona fills two urgent needs at once: reliable special Fire pressure and redirection through Rage Powder. It pairs naturally with Whimsicott’s Tailwind and Gholdengo’s spread damage, while Quiver Dance, Flame Body, and utility options give it value beyond opposing sun matchups. Its Rock weakness is manageable with Gyarados and future defensive additions, and 14 points leaves enough flexibility for the remaining six picks.

roster.name: Kingambit
roster.rationale: Kingambit gives the roster a durable physical win condition, powerful priority, and Defiant to punish the Intimidate-heavy opposing pool. Its Dark typing directly improves the Mega Gengar matchup while its Steel typing adds Fairy resistance and useful offensive pressure alongside Gholdengo, without requiring weather support. At 17 points, it leaves 23 points for five economical utility picks.

roster.name: Hatterene
roster.rationale: Hatterene gives the roster a valuable Trick Room mode alongside Kingambit, Gholdengo, and Gyarados while Magic Bounce improves the matchup into opposing Prankster disruption and status. Its strong special Fairy/Psychic pressure also helps against Fighting-types and can punish teams relying on Tailwind or setup. At 9 points, it preserves 14 points for four inexpensive complementary picks.

roster.name: Gliscor
roster.rationale: Gliscor is an excellent three-point utility pickup: its Ground immunity and Fighting resistance directly patch two of the roster’s biggest defensive concerns, while Poison Heal, Protect, Taunt, Helping Hand, and disruptive coverage give it flexible doubles sets. Although it adds another Rock weakness, its low cost preserves 11 points for three final picks, allowing us to pursue cheap speed control and support without sacrificing this important defensive profile.

roster.name: Aromatisse
roster.rationale: Aromatisse adds a dependable Trick Room mode alongside Hatterene while also offering After You, Helping Hand, Heal Pulse, and excellent anti-Taunt utility through Aroma Veil. Its Fairy overlap is acceptable because it provides a distinct slow-support role and improves matchups where Tailwind or Prankster disruption is unreliable, while costing 6 and leaving room for two inexpensive final picks.

roster.name: Meowstic-Female
roster.rationale: Meowstic-F is a legal two-point support pick that adds fast disruption, screens, Helping Hand, and Competitive pressure into Intimidate-heavy teams. It preserves three points for the final selection while complementing Whimsicott’s Tailwind role and Hatterene/Aromatisse’s slower modes without adding more Fire, Steel, or Fairy overlap.

roster.name: Passimian
roster.rationale: Passimian gives the roster a valuable Fighting-type attacker without adding another Fire, Steel, Fairy, or Rock weakness. Defiant punishes Intimidate and other stat drops, while Feint, Coaching, U-turn, Knock Off, and Rock Slide provide flexible doubles utility alongside Whimsicott Tailwind or Hatterene/Aromatisse Trick Room modes. Its Fighting pressure is especially useful against opposing Kingambit, Archaludon, Mega Tyranitar, and other Steel- or Dark-heavy teams.

roster.name: Mega Floette
roster.rationale: Mega Floette is the strongest remaining standalone centerpiece: Fairy Aura amplifies both its already elite 155 Special Attack and the pressure of any future Fairy partner, while 148 Special Defense and 102 Speed give it unusually reliable board presence. It is also flexible between immediate spread-pressure offense and a protected late-game Mega win condition, which matters greatly in open-sheet best-of-threes.

roster.name: Archaludon
roster.rationale: Archaludon is the best available partner for Mega Floette: it supplies a Steel/Dragon backbone, checks Poison and opposing Steel pressure into Floette, and creates an independently strong special-offense mode with excellent physical resilience through Stamina. At 19 points it exactly fits the current budget floor while denying a premium flexible centerpiece to the field.

roster.name: Sneasler
roster.rationale: Sneasler supplies the fast physical pressure this core lacks, with Fighting/Poison coverage that punishes the Steel, Dark, and Fairy structures already emerging. It is an excellent non-Mega offensive mode beside Mega Floette and forces respect even when Floette is not the chosen Mega evolution path.

roster.name: Talonflame
roster.rationale: Talonflame supplies the roster’s most important missing piece: immediate Gale Wings Tailwind, while also giving a Ground immunity and fast Fire/Flying pressure to protect Archaludon. It is a flexible support attacker with options such as Tailwind, Will-O-Wisp, Taunt, Brave Bird, and Flare Blitz, and its 15-point cost leaves enough budget for several excellent low-cost role players.

roster.name: Palafin
roster.rationale: Palafin is the strongest remaining Water-value pick: it supplies elite physical damage beside Mega Floette and Archaludon while offering a self-contained pivot plan through Flip Turn into Zero to Hero. Its low 12-point price still leaves enough budget to add a secondary Mega/Intimidate option plus several targeted utility pieces.

roster.name: Mega Manectric
roster.rationale: Mega Manectric is an exceptional 8-point alternate Mega: it supplies immediate post-Mega Intimidate, very high Speed, Electric pressure into Pelipper/Gyarados/Azumarill, and Volt Switch-style pivoting. It also gives the roster a distinct fast special mode when Mega Floette is awkward, while preserving enough budget for a 3+2+1+1 finish.

roster.name: Froslass
roster.rationale: Froslass is the best affordable immediate speed-control disruption piece: its naturally high Speed gives this roster a reliable Taunt into most Trick Room setters, while Icy Wind, Will-O-Wisp, Haze, Helping Hand, and screens give it real matchup-dependent flexibility. It also improves the Garchomp/Dragon-heavy matchups with Ice pressure without committing another Mega slot.

roster.name: Altaria
roster.rationale: Altaria is the best 1-point fit: Cloud Nine gives the roster a real weather-denial button into Charizard Y sun, Pelipper rain, and Tyranitar sand while its Flying typing adds another Ground immunity. It can also supply flexible support such as Tailwind, Haze, Safeguard, or disruptive Dragon/Flying pressure depending on the matchup.

roster.name: Banette
roster.rationale: Base Banette is a legal 1-point anti–Trick Room specialist with Taunt, Imprison + Trick Room, and Ghost typing to ignore Fake Out while executing its denial plan. It also contributes Will-O-Wisp, Destiny Bond, Disable, and Shadow Sneak as low-cost matchup utility.

roster.name: Furfrou
roster.rationale: Furfrou is the best remaining low-cost role compression: Fur Coat gives the roster a genuinely durable physical pivot, while Snarl, Charm, Helping Hand, Thunder Wave, and U-turn allow matchup-specific support sets. Its Ghost immunity also offers a useful defensive switch line into the several Ghost attackers present across the league.

teambuilds.rationale: We bring a sun-based core with Mega Charizard Y, Torkoal, and Venusaur, rounded out by Arcanine, Corviknight, and Basculegion-Male. Champions rules cap individual stats at 32 stat points and total team member points at 66, so our spreads are carefully adjusted. This team leverages Drought to power fire attacks and Chlorophyll speed, with Corviknight and Arcanine providing defensive and offensive presence.

The opponent brings a sand core with Mega Tyranitar and Excadrill, along with Dragapult and Rotom-Wash. We deploy our Sun team, using Charizard-Mega-Y to win the weather war against Sand Stream and pressure with Heat Wave. Venusaur utilizes Chlorophyll in sun to outspeed opponents and put threats to sleep. Torkoal resets sun and deals massive damage with Eruption. Basculegion punches through sand with Adaptability water attacks. Corviknight provides Tailwind support and physical defense, while Arcanine drops attack stats with Intimidate and cleans up with Extreme Speed.

This six pressures their Gengar, Scrafty, Toxapex, and Steel core with Kingambit, Passimian, and Hatterene while retaining strong answers to rain and Garchomp through Gyarados and Gholdengo. Whimsicott provides Prankster Tailwind, Encore, and Helping Hand for immediate tempo; Hatterene gives a slower Trick Room mode and Magic Bounce protection against disruption. Intimidate Gyarados and dual Fighting/Dark pressure make their physical attackers difficult to position safely.

Whimsicott enables immediate Prankster Tailwind while Gyarados can overwrite Drought with Rain Dance, protecting the team from the opponent's sun-boosted Fire core and powering Waterfall. Passimian and Gliscor pressure Aggron, Corviknight, and the Electric roster with Close Combat, Rock Slide, and Ground attacks, while Gholdengo provides spread Steel damage and Hatterene offers a slower Trick Room mode against Chlorophyll Venusaur and opposing speed control.

Bring both Megas for flexible Mega Manectric speed/Intimidate and Mega Floette Fairy Aura pressure; Manectric cleanly punishes Pelipper, while Floette threatens Garchomp, Scrafty, and Clefable. Talonflame supplies Tailwind and burns for their physical core, Sneasler gives immediate Fake Out and Poison pressure, and Archaludon plus Palafin provide resilient endgame options. Be careful deploying Palafin into a likely Mega Gengar lead, since Shadow Tag can deny its Zero to Hero pivot.

Mega Manectric is the primary Mega into Noivern, Gengar, and Mega Metagross, while Mega Floette is the alternate win condition when their Steel/Poison pressure is lighter. Talonflame supplies reliable priority Tailwind, Sneasler creates Fake Out turns for Palafin to transform, and Archaludon gives the squad a sturdy Fairy/Poison-resistant pivot with Snarl support. Preserve Palafin for the Hero-form endgame and use Manectric's post-Mega Intimidate to blunt Metagross, Incineroar, Azumarill, and Infernape.

Sand is uncontested — opponent has no weather setters, so TTar + Excadrill dominate speed tiers. Farigiraf's Armor Tail blanks all three of their Fake Out users (Incineroar, Infernape, Liepard) and gives a Trick Room pivot against their fast mode. Tinkaton's Mold Breaker Gigaton Hammer OHKOs Alcremie through Aroma Veil and ignores Aegislash's Stance Change. Rotom-Wash checks Azumarill and burns Metagross; Dragapult outruns everything and spreads burns or cleans up with Shadow Ball.

Rain team anchored by Mega Gengar's Shadow Tag, which traps and eliminates one non-Ghost opponent outright in doubles — removing Mega Floette, Palafin, or Mega Manectric from the fight entirely. Pelipper opens with Drizzle to power Surf and weaken opposing Fire moves (hurting Talonflame), then sets Tailwind so the whole team outspeeds the opponent's fast threats. Garchomp is immune to Electric attacks, sets Stealth Rock, and breaks physical walls with Earthquake. Clefable's Magic Guard and massive SpD wall Mega Floette's special assault while providing Wish/Light Screen support. Toxapex's Regenerator and 224 physical Defense shut down Sneasler and other physical attackers, while Toxic Spikes wear down non-Poison switch-ins. Meowscarada cleans up late-game with Protean-boosted coverage — Flower Trick (guaranteed crit), Sucker Punch (priority), and Brick Break (Fighting for Archaludon) — becoming faster than everything after Tailwind.

Opponent likely runs Gholdengo, Volcarona, Hatterene, Kingambit, Whimsicott, and a physical threat (Gyarados/Gliscor/Passimian). Mega Gengar with Shadow Tag is the linchpin — it traps and 2x-super-effectively hits Gholdengo with Shadow Ball while eliminating Hatterene. Pelipper sets rain via Drizzle + Damp Rock to neuter Volcarona's Fire STAB and power Hurricane at 100% accuracy. Clefable walls the many special attackers and sets 8-turn screens via Light Clay. Toxapex with Regenerator + Leftovers absorbs physical hits from Kingambit and Gyarados, while Toxic Spikes wear down switch-ins. Garchomp with Choice Scarf (~195 effective Speed) revenge-kills and breaks through with Earthquake (2x vs Kingambit). Meowscarada with Protean provides the fastest speed control, Dark Pulse for Psychic types, and U-turn momentum.

Sand core (Mega Tyranitar + Excadrill) overwrites their sun, denies Venusaur's Chlorophyll speed, and makes Excadrill the fastest mon on the field. Rotom-Wash and Dragapult answer Basculegion and apply special pressure; Tinkaton provides Fake Out support and a Fairy/Steel defensive pivot. Camerupt rounds out the six with Charcoal-boosted Fire moves to torch Venusaur and Corviknight, while Solid Rock helps it take an unexpected hit.

Opponent leans on Mega Floette's Fairy Aura nukes plus fast breakers (Sneasler, Talonflame, Palafin) and special pressure (Manectric, Archaludon). Incineroar's Intimidate + Fake Out and a Focus Sash Noivern lead stabilize the board with Tailwind, while Metagross and Aegislash (both resist Fairy; Aegislash is immune to Fighting) wall Floette and Sneasler and kill back with Steel hits. Azumarill (Belly Drum + Sitrus) and Eelektross (Life Orb Electric — the only super-effective answer to Palafin/Talonflame) are the offensive wincons, with Archaludon handled by Azumarill's Play Rough.

Rain team anchored by Mega Gengar's Shadow Tag trapping and absurd special offense (222 SpA, 200 Spe). Pelipper sets and extends rain with Damp Rock, also checking Noivern with Hurricane. Garchomp serves as the physical Dragon/Ground breaker, using Swords Dance and Earthquake to punish Mega Metagross, Incineroar, and Eelektross. Clefable is the special wall with Magic Guard, handling Noivern's Draco Meteor and spreading Thunder Wave speed control while Moonblast threatens Dark types. Meowscarada provides speed control at 192 Spe, revenge-kills Noivern with Sucker Punch, and deletes Azumarill with Energy Ball. Toxapex is the Regenerator physical tank absorbing Earthquakes and Gunk Shots, spreading Toxic Spikes to wear down switch-ins, and using Haze to shut down setup.

Opponent's sand core (Mega Tyranitar + Excadrill) threatens spread Earthquakes that would wreck most of my team, so I anchor on Noivern (Flying, immune) and Eelektross (Levitate, immune) as the only Ground-immune attackers and use Aegislash's Wide Guard to shield the rest. Azumarill (Belly Drum + Play Rough) and Mega Metagross (Meteor Mash) both OHKO/2HKO Tyranitar, while Eelektross's Grass Knot/Flamethrower and Aegislash's Shadow Ball/Flash Cannon clean up Excadrill and Dragapult. Incineroar's Intimidate + Will-O-Wisp + Shuca Berry blunt the physical sand attackers, and Noivern's Tailwind lets my slower wincons act ahead of Excadrill's Sand Rush.

Whimsicott provides Prankster Tailwind, Sunny Day to suppress sand-based speed and chip, and Encore disruption, while Hatterene's Magic Bounce plus Imprison-Trick Room blocks the opponent's alternate speed mode. Gyarados and Gliscor pressure Excadrill, Sandaconda, Camerupt, and Mega Tyranitar while covering each other's Ground weakness; Gholdengo handles the Steel/Fairy core, and Passimian gives immediate Fighting pressure into Mega Tyranitar and Excadrill.

Hex Appeal's Mega Gengar (Shadow Tag, 130 Spe, 170 SpA) is the top threat and is cleanly answered by Mega Metagross's Zen Headbutt, which survives Shadow Ball (~56 dmg) and OHKOs back; Liepard's Sucker Punch is priority backup. Incineroar's Intimidate plus Noivern's Tailwind (outspeeds the whole enemy tier at 236 Spe) control the physical/speed game, Azumarill's Huge Power Fairy/Water breaks Garchomp/Meowscarada and shrugs off Pelipper's rain, and Aegislash sets up behind King's Shield. Noivern's Ground immunity and Life Orb Boomburst cover Garchomp's Earthquake and the rain matchup.

Sand mode (TTar + Excadrill) is the primary engine: Sand Rush Excadrill hits 280 Speed and threatens Gholdengo/Volcarona/Kingambit with EQ and Iron Head, while TTar spams Rock Slide and removes items with Knock Off. Farigiraf's Armor Tail blanks Whimsicott's Prankster and its Trick Room reverses Hatterene/Aromatisse TR. Dragapult at 213 Speed revenge-kills with Spell Tag Shadow Ball and roasts Steels with Flamethrower. Rotom-Wash hard-walls Gyarados (guaranteed Thunderbolt OHKO) and threatens Gliscor with Hydro Pump, plus Will-O-Wisp for Kingambit. Tinkaton rounds it out with Fake Out pressure and Gigaton Hammer to OHKO Hatterene.

The opponent brings a fast offensive core featuring Sneasler, Talonflame, Palafin, and Mega Manectric, backed by Mega Floette and Archaludon. We leverage our sun infrastructure with Mega Charizard Y and Venusaur to out-offense and break down their defensive pieces, while Torkoal and Arcanine control the field and deter Sneasler/Talonflame. Corviknight and Basculegion round out the team to check physical attackers and clean up late game.

Altaria’s Cloud Nine is the central anti-sun piece: it disables Drought’s Fire and Chlorophyll boosts while enabling Palafin’s Water pressure. Mega Manectric checks Charizard Y, Corviknight, Basculegion, and the Electric-heavy backline, while Mega Floette supplies immediate special damage and Helping Hand support. Talonflame and Sneasler provide reliable disruption for setting Tailwind, pivoting Palafin into Hero form, and stopping slower Steel or Fire modes.
